records.query: How can C++ transfer exclusive ownership of an object?

documents.text: std::unique_ptr represents exclusive ownership and can transfer it with std::move.
std::shared_ptr shares ownership using a reference count.

records.query: Which standard algorithm sorts a range in place?

documents.text: std::sort orders the elements in the half-open range [first, last).
std::find searches a range for a value equal to the requested value.

records.query: How does a C++ mutex protect a critical section with RAII?

documents.text: std::lock_guard acquires a mutex at construction and releases it when the guard leaves scope.
std::atomic provides operations on a value that can be used safely between threads.

records.query: What prevents a null pointer from being used as a valid object pointer in modern C++?

documents.text: nullptr is the dedicated null pointer literal in modern C++.
std::optional represents a value that may be absent.
